questions.statement: Choose the correct preposition: 'The meeting starts ___ 9 a.m.'
questions.context: Semana W25 de ingles, grado 11: ejercicio 1 de 20 sobre prepositions of time at, in and on.

options.text: at
options.feedback: Correct! 'At' is used with exact clock times, and '9 a.m.' is a precise point in the day.

options.text: in
options.feedback: No. 'In' is used with longer periods such as months, years or parts of the day, not with a clock time.

options.text: on
options.feedback: No. 'On' is used with days and dates, not with the hour of the day.

options.text: for
options.feedback: No. 'For' measures duration, so it would answer for how long rather than at what time.

questions.explanation:
'At' is used with exact clock times, and '9 a.m.' is a precise point in the day. In this item the choice that works is 'at', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.

questions.statement: Which sentence uses 'in' correctly with a period of time?
questions.context: Semana W25 de ingles, grado 11: ejercicio 2 de 20 sobre prepositions of time at, in and on.

options.text: The storm arrived in December and caused damage across the island.
options.feedback: Correct! Months are long periods, and English uses 'in' before the name of a month.

options.text: The storm arrived at December and caused damage across the island.
options.feedback: No. 'At' is used for clock times and for specific points, not for the name of a month.

options.text: The storm arrived on December and caused damage across the island.
options.feedback: No. 'On' is used with days and dates, so it is not the preposition for a month.

options.text: The storm arrived for December and caused damage across the island.
options.feedback: No. 'For' would measure the length of time the storm lasted, not the period in which it arrived.

questions.explanation:
Months are long periods, and English uses 'in' before the name of a month. In this item the choice that works is 'The storm arrived in December and caused damage across the island.', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.

questions.context: Semana W25 de ingles, grado 11: ejercicio 3 de 20 sobre prepositions of time at, in and on.

options.text: on
options.feedback: Correct! Full dates take 'on', because a specific day of a specific month is being named.

options.text: in
options.feedback: No. 'In' would be correct for the month or the year alone, but not for a full date.

options.text: at
options.feedback: No. 'At' is used with clock times and with particular points in space, not with dates.

options.text: by
options.feedback: No. 'By' expresses a deadline or a limit, which has no place in this sentence.

questions.explanation:
Full dates take 'on', because a specific day of a specific month is being named. In this item the choice that works is 'on', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.

questions.context: Semana W25 de ingles, grado 11: ejercicio 4 de 20 sobre prepositions of time at, in and on.

options.text: The library closes early on Sundays during the summer.
options.feedback: Correct! Days of the week take 'on' in English, so 'on Sundays' is the correct form.

options.text: The library closes early in Sundays during the summer.
options.feedback: No. 'In' is used for months, years and parts of the day, not for a day of the week.

options.text: The library closes early at Sundays during the summer.
options.feedback: No. 'At' is used with clock times; no hour is named in this sentence.

options.text: The library closes early for Sundays during the summer.
options.feedback: No. 'For Sundays' would measure duration across several Sundays rather than naming the day.

questions.explanation:
Days of the week take 'on' in English, so 'on Sundays' is the correct form. In this item the choice that works is 'The library closes early on Sundays during the summer.', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the correct preposition with a part of the day?
questions.context: Semana W25 de ingles, grado 11: ejercicio 6 de 20 sobre prepositions of time at, in and on.

options.text: The shop opens early in the morning and closes late at night.
options.feedback: Correct! 'In' is used with parts of the day such as the morning, while 'at' is used with 'night'.

options.text: The shop opens early at the morning and closes late in the night.
options.feedback: No. 'At the morning' is not used; 'the morning' needs 'in', though 'at night' takes no article.

options.text: The shop opens early on the morning and closes late at the night.
options.feedback: No. 'On the morning' is not the standard form; English uses 'in the morning'.

options.text: The shop opens early of the morning and closes late of the night.
options.feedback: No. 'Of' is not a preposition of time and cannot introduce these expressions.

questions.explanation:
'In' is used with parts of the day such as the morning, while 'at' is used with 'night'. In this item the choice that works is 'The shop opens early in the morning and closes late at night.', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.

options.text: The workshop lasted two hours and began at four in the afternoon.
options.feedback: Correct! 'For' or the bare plural expresses duration, and 'at' marks the starting point in time.

options.feedback: No. 'At two hours' would mark a clock time, but the sentence states a length of two hours, not a point.

options.feedback: No. 'In two hours' would mean 'after two hours have passed', which is a different meaning.

options.text: The workshop lasted on two hours and began in four in the afternoon.
options.feedback: No. 'On two hours' and 'in four in the afternoon' both use the wrong prepositions for duration and for the afternoon.

questions.explanation:
'For' or the bare plural expresses duration, and 'at' marks the starting point in time. In this item the choice that works is 'The workshop lasted two hours and began at four in the afternoon.', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.
